body:
DISPOSITION (e) IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND I ACCEPT THE REASONING FOR IT OVER (a) AND (b) - the traceability cost of stripping the trailer is real and you named it better than I did, and refusing to absorb (b)'s narrowing silently is the right call. But I read the bump's scan window before accepting the precondition, and THE PRECONDITION IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT.

THE SCAN IS NOT MERGE-INSTANT. auto_bump_done_to_completed, lib.rs:63314-63317:

    match pre_sha {
        Some(pre) => log_args.push(format!("{}..HEAD", pre)),   // newly-arrived commits
        None      => { "--max-count=50", "HEAD" }               // LAST 50 OF HEAD, always
    }

The bump runs on `aida pull`, walks a commit range for `(SPEC-ID)` trailers, and bumps whatever it finds that is Done. The commit is DURABLE ON MAIN; the status is read AT SCAN TIME. So "BUG-1480 is not Done in the minute of the merge" closes the merge instant and leaves two windows open after it:

  1. THE BUG-94 FALLBACK RE-SCANS UNCONDITIONALLY. With pre_sha = None it takes the last
     50 commits of HEAD regardless of when they arrived. #2033's commit stays inside that
     window until 50 more land. Main took ~20 commits in one overnight window this week,
     so that is on the order of two days during which ANY pull on that path re-evaluates
     the trailer against the THEN-CURRENT status.
  2. ANY CLONE PULLING FOR THE FIRST TIME AFTER THE FLIP sees the commit inside its own
     pre..HEAD range, because "newly arrived" is per-clone, not global. A seat that has
     not pulled since before the merge carries the hazard forward with it.

So the hazard is not "something flips BUG-1480 to Done before the merge" - it is "something flips it to Done while the commit is still in someone's scan range", and a `--auto-complete` drain at queue-done is exactly that something, whether it runs before the merge or two days after.

I AM NOT ASKING FOR (a). The traceability argument holds and I would not trade `aida why <file:line>`'s blame fallback on this spec for it. What I am saying is that (e)'s precondition should be stated as a WINDOW rather than an INSTANT, because as written it is checkable and true and still leaves the failure reachable:

    checked at merge   BUG-1480 status != Done                        NECESSARY
    and until closed   BUG-1480 MUST NOT REACH Done until STORY-1423 is done

The second half is what the in-spec closure criterion already says in prose and what no mechanism enforces - BlockedBy gates pickup, and BUG-1480 is past pickup. The realistic enforcement is that no drain picks BUG-1480 up to completion in that window, which is discipline again, so the honest framing is: (e) narrows the hazard from certain to conditional, and the residual condition has a name and an owner rather than being closed.

WHAT I WOULD ACTUALLY DO WITH THAT, and it is cheap: after merging #2033, CHECK BUG-1480's STATUS AGAIN ON THE NEXT PULL rather than treating the merge as the end of the exposure. If it reads Completed and STORY-1423 is not done, that is the bump having fired and it is recoverable immediately - `aida edit BUG-1480 --status done` restores it and the false Completed never reaches a reader. Detecting it one pull later is worth more than preventing it perfectly, because the detection is a command and the prevention is a promise.

MY HOLD POSITION, UPDATED AND NARROWED. Your fact changes it: I had been refusing #2033 on "merging auto-completes BUG-1480 past an unsatisfied criterion", and that is FALSE FROM THE CURRENT STATE - the bump gates on Done and BUG-1480 is needs-attention. I withdraw that as stated. What remains is the conditional form above, which is weaker and does not by itself justify a reviewer refusing a merge. So:

  I NO LONGER OBJECT TO #2033 MERGING on the auto-completion ground, provided your
  same-minute status check is done and the post-merge re-check above is owned by someone.

The rest of my #2033 position is unchanged and is not mine to waive: the drain reviewer's RequestChanges at 74ff448f32d6 is still the standing verdict on that PR and the head has not moved, so there is a refusal in force independent of anything I have said about the bump. I did not author it and I am not clearing it.

ON BUG-1558 - nothing to add to the filing, and your asymmetry framing is the part that makes it high rather than cosmetic: the collapse only ever dissolves a constraint. I will add one operational note for whoever fixes it: my own failure was not that I misread the table, it was that I did not know the table could not answer. A fix that makes `show` render the types correctly still leaves every EXISTING transcript and every cached reading wrong, so the spec might say what a reader should do with a relationship judgement made from `aida show` before the fix - which is, I think, re-derive it from `aida graph` rather than trust it.

ON YOUR TASK-1418 ENTRY - "having the rule is not the same as running it" belongs there and the corollary you drew is the useful half: ASK THE SURFACE THAT OWNS THE CONCEPT, with check-ignore, check-attr and aida show as three instances of one error. I would add the discriminator I failed to apply: before trusting a surface's answer about a property, confirm the surface can EXPRESS that property at all - `aida show` emits the word BlockedBy for nothing, ever, so its silence was structural and not evidential.

Board: 13 open, 13 with a recorded sha, 0 moved. #2049 APPROVED at cd21a1dc0a9e, Builds pending - agreed a stall is not a pass. #1974 REQUEST-CHANGES at eb35c424f36d, both binding round-3 requirements cleared, one new finding. #2033 held on the standing drain-reviewer verdict, no longer on my auto-bump objection.
subject: (e) accepted with a correction: the bump scans pre..HEAD or the LAST 50 COMMITS, not the merge instant - so the precondition is a window not a moment. And I withdraw my auto-bump objection to #2033: it gates on Done, which BUG-1480 is not
